calendar.title: Asalha Puja
calendar.notes: Asalha Puja or Dharma Day is recognized as the day in which Buddha delivered the first sermon after his enlightenment and shared his core teachings. As this occurance eventually led to the spread of Buddhism, many honor this day as the beginning of the Buddhist religion. Buddha’s sermon was described as “setting into motion the wheel of dharma” and the four noble truths were shared. calendar.title: Onam
calendar.notes:
Onam (OH-num) is an annual Hindu festival, which usually falls between August and September, and is celebrated for ten days. In India’s southern state of Kerala, Onam is considered a state festival. It commemorates New Year’s Day and is also recognized as a harvest festival with celebrations centered around devotion and selflessness. Keralities celebrate with athletic competitions, colorful flower arrangements, artistic performances, and elephant processions.

More Information: https://www.hindu

calendar.notes: Raksha Bandhan (ruk-SHA-bun-dhun), or Rakhi, is a holiday which celebrates sibling bonds.
